subject: Synapse MAP: unit-price verification & eval runbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@synapsehealth.com>, procurement@synapsehealth.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-01-12T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Synapse MAP kickoff — unit economics checkpoints and eval plan

Emma / Synapse procurement team — thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attaching a draft MAP and a small sample of anonymized traffic we use for early econ checks. Key asks to close the MAP without surprises: a) confirm representative traffic profile (tokens per request, % of long-context flows), b) agree acceptance criteria for the eval run (latency SLO, 95p token latency, quality pass-rate on 150 eval prompts), and c) procurement timeline for a pilot credit / PO so we can schedule Dedicated capacity for the run.

Short summary of the unit-econ items we discussed:
- Baseline token assumptions: ~30 in / 220 out for standard lookup flows; 120 / 800 on long consult queries (we highlighted where caching helps).
- Caching: prefix caching expected to hit ~30% for our sample traffic; we recommend enabling prefix cache on route and setting TTL=10m for session reuse.
- Batching: recommend starting with dynamic batching (max batch size 32, target latency budget 180ms) for noninteractive endpoints; for interactive chat keep batch size=1 and use KV cache.

Attachments: synapse_map_draft_v3.pdf (MAP with milestones), traffic_sample_anon.csv (sample traffic used for tokenization), eval-harness-instructions.md (how to run the harness and smoke tests).

Can you confirm timeline constraints from procurement (target PO date) and whether the sample traffic looks representative? If you prefer, we'll run a short gated simulation on hosted API first to validate tokens/$ before scheduling Dedicated.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — the MAP looks comprehensive. Two quick clarifying questions so procurement can model the costs correctly:
1) When you quote tokens/$ in the MAP, is that before or after applying caching and batching? We need both a raw token rate and an "operational" tokens-per-dollar assuming your recommended caching/batching profile.
2) For the long consult queries (800 tokens out), do you expect KV cache to reduce repeated token generation across follow-ups, or do you expect most of that traffic to be unique?

Procurement is aiming for an internal review next Tue (1/20). We may be able to issue a PO by 1/23 if commercial terms are unchanged. If you have an estimate of credits required to run the evaluation for 2 weeks at our projected volume (shown in the attached CSV), that will help.

—Emma
Emma Li
Head of Product, Synapse Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@synapsehealth.com>, procurement@synapsehealth.com
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Synapse MAP kickoff — unit economics checkpoints and eval plan

Emma — good questions. Short answers first, then details.
- Tokens/$: the MAP includes both (a) raw unit price for the model variant we recommended (tokens/$ without optimizations) and (b) a modeled tokens-per-dollar using our recommended caching + batching profile. The "operational" numbers in the draft assume prefix caching hit-rate=30% and batching for noninteractive of 24 reqs/batch.
- Long consults + KV: for those flows KV cache helps across a session (repeated context reuse) but not across unique patient consults. We expect KV to reduce token generation for multi-turn sessions by ~20–35% depending on session length.

Estimated credits for a 2-week eval at the sample volume: about 3,500 USD of credits to cover Hosted API runs (includes test harness runs, 2 daily end-to-end runs, and a 48h peak soak). If you want to validate on Dedicated we can provide the same harness but need a short reservation window (48–72h).

Links: eval harness (hosted) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SynapseEval
Quick simulation script: eval-harness-instructions.md (attached).

Ben — can you confirm pilot credit approval workflow and whether sales can pre-approve the $3.5k credit under the standard pilot package?

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Synapse MAP kickoff — unit economics checkpoints and eval plan

Emma / team — hi, Marissa on the Ops side. Below is a short eval plan I propose; it's split into measurement (what we quantify) and acceptance (what Synapse signs off on). I'd like your confirmation on representative endpoints from the CSV so we run the right tests.

Eval plan (high level):
- Day 0: verify traffic ingestion and tokenization (we run a token breakdown on your sample CSV).
- Days 1–3: hosted smoke runs to validate functional parity for 50 canonical prompts (verify quality pass-rate >= 85%).
- Days 4–7: soak test at 2x expected peak for 4-hour windows to measure batching behavior and latency tail. Collect: tokens consumed, average batch size, 50/95/99 p token latencies.
- Days 8–12: run Dedicated pilot (if PO/procurement confirmed) or continue hosted simulation. Measure cost per 100k tokens (raw) and effective tokens/$ after cache+batches.

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- 95p token latency <= 250ms for interactive flows, <= 500ms for bulk inference with batching enabled.
- Effective tokens per dollar within 15% of MAP projection (we will provide lower/upper bounds).
- Quality regression: <3% drop vs baseline prompts on named intent set.

Operational notes:
- Please supply a minimal anonymized session sample with repeat-turns annotated (we can use the CSV format we've attached). That lets us estimate KV reuse more accurately.
- We'll run the tokenized breakdown and share a short report by EOD Day 1.

Attachments: I'll attach the runbook snippets to the shared drive folder; see eval-harness-instructions.md for exact commands.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
